doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sadik Hakim, also called Dense or Argonne Thornton
summary: Brown and Haynes sort out the pianist's names and that he is not Omar Hakim's father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: How did that come out? How did that work out?
It worked out good.
I mean, how did that come to – how did you – how did that work?
Dense Thornton – Sadik Hakim – was playing piano in there.
Argonne Thornton?
Yeah.
What did you call him?
Dense Thornton.
Dense
D-e-n-s-e. I think that was his first name, before Sadik Hakim. Dense. On some records it says Dense Thornton. I knew him around 52nd Street as Dense.
That’s Omar’s . . .
That’s what?
That’s Omar Hakim’s father.
Right – no, no, no. That’s another guy. The trombone player is Omar’s father, not . . .
Sadik Hakim, no? We’re worry about that later. We’ll clean that up.
Another Hakim is the father. It’s not the same guy. He plays trombone. Dense didn’t – I don’t think Dense had any kids. If he did . . .
[Omar Hakim is the son of the trombonist Hasaan Hakim.]
I thought his name was Argonne Thornton.
Yeah, Argonne. Maybe Dense was his nickname.
Okay.
Argonne was his real name. You got me on that one. But yeah, he didn’t have – if he did have kids, they wouldn’t be all black, because he loved blond ladies. Can you keep that in there?
Sure.
I think I might have a taste. Go ahead brother.
